title: Voice mode can open duplicate WebSockets during normal re-renders
reasoning: connectWebSocket only treats an OPEN socket as already connected. A socket in CONNECTING state is not protected, so a later effect pass can create another WebSocket and overwrite websocketRef. That effect is especially prone to rerun because useAudioCaptureRefs returns new setter functions every render, which flow into start/stop/shutdown callback dependencies. The prior CONNECTING socket can still open, send the language payload, and remain connected without being tracked by websocketRef, creating duplicate backend clients and leaked transcription connections.
reproduction: Enable voice mode in a component that re-renders while the first WebSocket is still CONNECTING. The enabled effect runs again, connectWebSocket creates a second socket because the first is not OPEN, and the first socket is no longer reachable through websocketRef.
recommendation: Treat CONNECTING as an existing connection, or close any previous non-CLOSED socket before replacing websocketRef. Also make the ref setter callbacks stable with useCallback or avoid putting unstable setter wrappers into callback dependency chains.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are listed for this source group, and the package test command is generic Jest with no included voice hook coverage.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a hook test with a mock WebSocket that remains CONNECTING across a re-render while enabled is true, then assert only one WebSocket instance is created and only one language payload can be sent.
minimumFixScope: useVoiceMode connectWebSocket guard plus stabilizing useAudioCaptureRefs setter identity or removing those setters from unstable dependency chains.
